pr_title: Make chat labels configurable in mod.yaml
pr_body:
This PR:
- Removes hard-coded chat labels and makes them configurable in `mod.yaml` as `IGlobalModData` (this includes the labels for the "Team/All" chat toggle button)
- Adds a method overload for `AddSystemLine` that omits the `name` parameter to reduce duplication (this is in a separate commit but I will squash it if need be)
- TESTCASE changes the labels in D2k mod like this and removes "Mentat" strings hard-coded in lua scripts:
```yaml
ChatLabels:
	BattlefieldControl: Mentat
	Mission: Mentat
	Debug: Developer
	All: Everyone
	Spectators: Observers
	Team: Allies
	Ally: Friendly
	Spectator: Observer
	Dead: Defeated
```

Closes #17551
pr_comments: Updated description of lua API methods. I will squash the fixup commit when merge-ready.
Do we want to have the testcase merged as well?

> Do we want to have the testcase merged as well?

This part and the lua changes seem worthy:
```yaml
ChatLabels:
	BattlefieldControl: Mentat
	Mission: Mentat
```

Alright, I have gathered some context on the chrome strings. They are all over the place and preparing them for localization would be a huge undertaking...

But in the process I realized that the aim of this PR was to **make some strings configurable** (_"Battlefield Control"_ and _"Mission"_). And I have gone a bit too far by including other strings which are probably better left hard-coded (labels for _"Team"_, _"All"_, _"Spectators"_, _"Debug"_, etc.). 

And then there is the conceptual problem - making strings configurable is very different to making strings translatable. I mean, a string should be translatable without being configurable. Otherwise we'd have to extract every single chrome string into yaml (via `IGlobalModData` or another mechanism) and we'd end up with a big pile of strings... a sort of dumping ground. And the logic parts would be filled with references to the strings instead of the real thing. Which means that blocks of code would change from this:
```csharp
ConfirmationDialogs.ButtonPrompt(
					title: "Leave Mission",
					text: "Leave this game and return to the menu?",
```

to something like that:

```csharp
ConfirmationDialogs.ButtonPrompt(
					title: ChromeStrings.ButtonLeaveMission,
					text: ChromeStrings.PromptLeaveMission,
```

which IMO looks very cryptic and unintuitive.

I would rather leave the hard-coded strings in place but wrap them in a some function to make them translatable:
```csharp
// pseudo-code
ConfirmationDialogs.ButtonPrompt(
					title: Translate("Leave Mission", context: "button-label"),
					text: Translate("Leave this game and return to the menu?"),
```

Unless of course we want to **make all chrome strings configurable** :thinking: I don't know what are the practices for i18n in the C# world and what is the plan for OpenRA. I have experience only with gettext in the PHP world. But I know that i18n is very hard to get right even with the proper tools.

I think we should come up with a plan for how we're going to handle configurability and/versus translatability of strings before moving on with this PR.
now that I think about it, the idea was something just like that, but hardcoding string ids instead of text, so english is a translation just like any other.

OK, so it's a combination of the two, something like this, where context is inferred from the string ID:
```csharp
Translate(stringId: "ButtonLabelAllChat");
Translate(stringId: "ButtonLabelTeamChat");
Translate(stringId: "ChatLabelSystem");
Translate(stringId: "ChatLabelTeam");
```

With such approach string customization and translation would be handled in the same place. So for example in order to change the chat labels in D2k we would add a version of the English translation that goes something like:
```yaml
ChatLabelSystem: "Mentat"
ChatLabelMission: "Mentat"
```

In that case `mod.yaml` is not the right place for these strings. Where would the default versions of the strings live? And we should integrate some translation framework (to handle grammar, plurals, etc.) - I saw a mention of Fluent (see https://github.com/OpenRA/OpenRA/issues/10475#issuecomment-401598016). 

I think it's better to shelve this PR until we got an idea of how to handle translation.

issue_context.title: "Battlefield Control" chat label is hard-coded
issue_context.body: "Battlefield Control" chat label is always used with `AddSystemLine` but it's hard-coded in all of the function calls. Mods may want do define their own system chat label.

review_comments:
These prefixes are missing important context that might lead to them being (mis)used in other contexts, which might lead to them breaking when eventually translated.

Can we use `AllChat` (`ChatAll`?), `TeamChat`, etc?

Yes, good point. The context comes from them being under the `ChatLabels` class but that context probably does not carry over to the translation framework (I should get familiar with that). So without that actually all of them are missing context and can be misused. 

What about a more generic `Labels` (`UILabels`?, `ChromeLabels`?) class and then giving each label context: `ChatMission`, `ChatDebug`, etc.

Ah, I see. I missed the class name here.

Giving this a more generic name (`UILogicStrings`?), and future PRs migrating additional hardcoded strings, would provide a framework for solving the second core point blocking #10475.
I'm on board with getting rid of hard-coded strings and making them translatable. I will look around the code for other strings and give this a little more thought.
:+1: to taking a look to get more context and tweaking this if appropriate to prepare, but IMO this PR should stay focused on the "Battlefield Control" label, leaving the scope creep to later PRs.
